তারিখ : ২৬ জ্যৈষ্ঠ, ১৪১৮ বঙ্গাব্দ/০৯ জুন, ২০১১ খ্রিস্টাব্দ।

এস,আর,ও নং ১৬৫-আইন/২০১১/২৩৫২/কাস্টমস।- Customs Act, 1969 (Act IV of 1969) এর section 219, উক্ত Act এর Third Schedule এর Item 17 এর সহিত পাঠ্যব্য, এ প্রদত্ত ক্ষমতাবলে জাতীয় রাজস্ব বোর্ড, যাত্রী (অপযটক) ব্যাগেজ (আমদানি) বিধিমালা, ২০১০ বাতিলক্রমে, নিম্নরূপ বিধিমালা প্রণয়ন করিল, যথা:-

Customs Act 1969: This act provides the enabling legal authority under Section 219 and Item 17 of the Third Schedule for the National Board of Revenue to frame rules concerning baggage import.
The legislation serves as the foundational parent statute for the issuance of new baggage rules and the repeal of previous ones.
National Board of Revenue: The board is the empowered government body authorized to formulate and issue customs-related regulations under the Customs Act 1969.
Passenger (Non-Tourist) Baggage (Import): These specific rules are repealed by the National Board of Revenue through this notification to pave the way for the introduction of new baggage regulations.
Third Schedule: Item 17 of this schedule is read in conjunction with Section 219 of the Customs Act 1969 to authorize the regulatory framework for baggage imports.

Passenger (Non-Tourist) Baggage (Import): This set of rules is officially designated as the Passenger (Non-Tourist) Baggage (Import) Rules 2011.
These rules apply to all passengers except for those specifically governed under the Tourist Baggage (Import) Rules 1981 and the Privileged Persons (Customs Procedures) Rules 2003.
Tourist Baggage (Import) Rules 1981: These rules establish a distinct regulatory framework for tourists, and the Passenger (Non-Tourist) Baggage (Import) Rules 2011 do not apply to individuals covered by this instrument.
Privileged Persons (Customs Procedures): These rules provide specific customs procedures for privileged persons, who are explicitly excluded from the application of the Passenger (Non-Tourist) Baggage (Import) Rules 2011.

Baggage: Baggage is defined as reasonable quantities of food, clothing, household, or other personal items imported by a passenger.
Passenger: A passenger is defined as any person arriving from abroad.
Schedule: The term schedule refers to any schedule attached to these rules.

এসিস্ট্যান্ট রেভিনিউ অফিসার অব কাস্টমস্ এর স্বাক্ষর (নামীয় সীলসহ)

সহকারী/উপ-কমিশনার (Assistant/Deputy Commissioner of Customs) এর স্বাক্ষর (নামীয় সীলসহ)

Passenger Baggage: Passengers arriving by air or sea who are at least twelve years old are allowed to import specific quantities of personal baggage, including hand luggage and checked items up to a defined weight or size limit, without payment of duties and taxes.
Additional personal effects like clothing, books, and study materials are permitted duty-free within specified weight limits.

Passengers under twelve years of age are entitled to duty-free clearance of personal baggage only up to a single container of a specific weight or size limit, and are excluded from other baggage allowances.
Unaccompanied baggage may be cleared duty-free if a declaration is submitted on the prescribed form and conforms to the rules, provided a copy of the declaration is submitted to the customs officer.
Passenger Baggage Declaration Form: A declaration form must be submitted to the customs officer for the clearance of unaccompanied baggage.
A specific form is provided in the schedule for the purchase of goods from the designated duty-free city sales center, which must be completed by the passenger and certified by customs officials.
Assistant/Deputy/Joint Commissioner of C: This official is authorized to sign and validate the purchase form for goods acquired by passengers from the designated city sales center.
Assistant Commissioner of Customs: The Assistant Revenue Officer is tasked with verifying and signing the passenger declaration for goods purchased within the permitted timeframe after arrival.
Customs Authority: Customs officers are responsible for determining the availability and eligibility of goods declared by passengers for purchase from designated city sales centers, ensuring coordination with items already imported by the passenger.

Passenger Baggage Allowance: Passengers arriving via land routes are permitted to import baggage free of all customs duties and taxes up to a designated maximum monetary limit, regardless of the duration of their stay abroad.

Passenger Baggage Allowance: Passengers arriving via air, water, or land routes who are elderly, sick, or disabled are permitted to import medical equipment and wheelchairs free of all duties and taxes.

Airline Crew Baggage Allowance: Bangladeshi crew or officers on international flights arriving in Bangladesh may import baggage up to a specified monetary value without paying any customs duties or taxes.
Seafarer Baggage Allowance: Bangladeshi crew or officers arriving at a Bangladeshi seaport from a foreign port may import baggage up to a specified monetary value duty-free.
Upon signing off from their duties, seafarers are permitted to import baggage up to a higher specified value subject to the payment of all applicable customs duties and taxes.
Transport Crew Baggage Allowance: Drivers and stewards of passenger buses arriving from abroad are allowed to import personal items including clothing, bedding, and food duty-free, along with additional personal and household goods up to a specified monetary limit.

Green Channel: Passengers who are not carrying any dutiable or taxable goods are permitted to use the Green Channel at the airport.
Customs officers have the authority to perform random scanning and examination of a limited percentage of passengers passing through the Green Channel.
Customs officers may conduct a scan and examination of the baggage of any passenger using the Green Channel if there is a reasonable suspicion.
Red Channel: The Red Channel is designated for use by passengers carrying goods that are subject to customs duty and taxes.
Customs Authority: Customs officers are authorized to select a specific percentage of passengers using the Green Channel for random baggage screening.
Customs officers maintain the right to inspect and scan any passenger's baggage at their discretion based on reasonable suspicion, regardless of channel selection.

For unaccompanied baggage, the passenger must submit a declaration to the customs authority prior to exiting the customs hall or customs area.
If a declaration cannot be made upon arrival due to unavoidable circumstances, it may be submitted within a specified timeframe to an officer not below the rank of Assistant Commissioner of Customs.
Passenger Baggage Declaration Form: This is the official form prescribed under the rules for passengers to declare their personal belongings, jewelry, precious metals, currency, and other dutiable or non-dutiable items upon arrival.

The form requires comprehensive details including passenger identity, travel history, information on accompanied and unaccompanied baggage, and specific disclosures regarding high-value items like gold, silver, alcohol, tobacco, and foreign currency.
Assistant/Deputy/Joint Commissioner of C: This officer is the minimum authorized authority to accept a delayed baggage declaration if the passenger was unable to file it upon arrival due to unavoidable reasons.
National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue is the authority responsible for prescribing the standard baggage declaration form to be used by all arriving passengers.
Baggage: Passengers are subject to specific limitations and requirements when importing unaccompanied baggage, which is restricted to a set frequency per calendar year.

Commercial Baggage Import: Passengers importing goods in commercial quantities or goods exceeding established limits are subject to customs duty and tax assessment.
Such imports may require clearance from the Chief Controller of Imports and Exports.
Clearance is contingent upon the payment of all applicable duties, taxes, and penalties determined through the adjudication process.
Adjudication of Customs Cases: Adjudication is the mandatory legal mechanism for determining the customs duty, taxes, and penalties due on baggage imported in commercial quantities.
Schedule 2: This schedule lists specific categories of personal and household items that are subject to prescribed duties and taxes when imported as baggage.
It includes items such as home appliances, electronic equipment, precious metals, and cameras used for professional purposes.
Schedule 3: This schedule provides a list of personal and household goods that are eligible for import as baggage free of all customs duties and taxes.
It includes essential home appliances, communication devices, and personal electronics within specified limits.
Chief Controller of Imports and Exports: The Chief Controller of Imports and Exports is the authority responsible for issuing clearances for baggage imports that fall under the commercial category.
